note.text: A timetable organises activities into realistic periods. Begin with fixed commitments, including school, travel, chores, meals and rest. Add study periods that match your priorities and available energy. Allow transitions and breaks. A timetable is a plan to review, not a claim that every learner has identical responsibilities or resources. Use headings and consistent time notation so another person can understand it.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A timetable organises activities into realistic periods. Begin with fixed commitments, including school, travel, chores, meals and rest. sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Draft schedule: After the journey home, I complete the agreed household task. I then revise one topic, take a short break and practise questions. After the evening meal, I check the next day's books. I leave time for rest and adjust the plan when a task takes longer.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: List fixed commitments before choosing optional tasks. Check that periods do not overlap and that the total fits the available time. Review the plan after trying it; do not promise that a timetable alone guarantees success.

questions.prompt: An imaginary study period begins at {start}:00 and ends at {end}:00 on the same afternoon. How many minutes are available?

misconceptions.explain: That is the number of hours; the answer requested is in minutes.
Use the difference between end and start, not their sum.

paper_task.prompt: Draw a personal or imaginary after-school timetable in your exercise book. Show fixed commitments, study, transitions and rest. Keep private household details fictional if preferred.
model: Draft schedule: After the journey home, I complete the agreed household task. I then revise one topic, take a short break and practise questions. After the evening meal, I check the next day's books. I leave time for rest and adjust the plan when a task takes longer.
checklist: My time periods are clear and do not overlap.
I have allowed for chores, travel, meals and rest.
I have identified a change to make if the plan proves unrealistic.
